newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-Valeo sees profit, debt rising.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Valeo sees profit, debt rising.

text.p: Car parts supplier Valeo expects both its debt and profits to rise this year, chairman Noel Goutard said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
He said the company's financial position was solid and could allow for a substantial acquisition.
Valeo reported on Wednesday that first-half net attributable profit rose 12.8 percent to 740 million francs on sales of 17.26 billion, up 14.6 percent.
"We are targeting sales exceeding 32 billion, that is plus 13 percent for the year," Goutard told RFTV. "Also, we expect to be able to register a much better net result for 1997."
Valeo's net debt rose to 808 million francs in the first half of 1997 from 673 million a year earlier, while equity rose to 11.55 billion from 10.56 billion.
"We believe that we might reach and exceed somewhat one billion francs in net debt before the end of the year, but this is well invested in the restructuring programme in Europe," Goutard said.

The company has been active this year, buying up Brazil's leading manufacturer of car door handles, locks and anti-theft systems Univel, concluding a joint venture in China to make clutches, and forming a clutch venture in India.

"Basically we are targeting as a priority North America but you have to find the right opportunity, and also acquisitions in North America in the auto component industry are quite sky high in terms of price. If the market slows down, prices for new acquisitions in the U.S. might be more reasonable," he said.

Goutard said he expected Valeo to remain a favourite among U.S. pension funds, who own around 70 percent of the shares, because the company has a clear strategy. "We are focused on the auto industry. We have a strong strategy of growth, profitable growth," he said.

But he said the share's evolution also hinges on the bourse trends. "I think there is a little overheating and that may translate into a slowdown and we are very dependent on that, too," Goutard said.
